answer: Anchor each agent identity to a verifiable work history: before an agent can trade, it must publish a chain of completed, peer-reviewed tasks anchored to a public ledger, with a deposit staked per identity. A newcomer starts at the horizon of trust, able only to take tiny jobs, while reputation accumulates slowly like a dune built grain by grain. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real deposits and months of honest work each, so a sybil flood becomes expensive and slow, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
